registered: 2026-08-18, BEFORE the cohort-calibrated R1 is run
question: R1 failed because the engine calibrates on COUNTRY means, which carry no within-country information. The ported cohort solver (calibration.calibrate_cohort) fits POLITICAL x AGE cells instead. Does that rescue within-country prediction, or are the 18 features structurally incapable of it?

arms.R1_country: current: fit the engine on the national share, score later years (measured 0.1557)
arms.R1_cohort: fit calibrate_cohort on POLITICAL cohort cells (pol_far_left .. pol_far_right) at the fit year, score the same later years
arms.fair_anchor: year-1 persistence, 0.1158 — the honest baseline the engine must beat

REGISTERED EXPECTATIONS.primary: cohort calibration IMPROVES on 0.1557 but still LOSES to the 0.1158 fair anchor — because the 18 features are identical for every American, so no fitting resolution can manufacture within-country variance that the features do not contain
REGISTERED EXPECTATIONS.surprise_branch: if cohort calibration BEATS 0.1158, the features do carry within-country signal that country-mean fitting was discarding, and the within-country claim reopens
REGISTERED EXPECTATIONS.null_branch: if cohort calibration is indistinguishable from country calibration, that is direct evidence the fitting resolution is irrelevant and the constraint is the feature set

why_it_matters: this decides whether 'cross-national instrument only' is a permanent architectural boundary or an artifact of how we fit.
